rounds.text: RR Kabel Ltd is backed by exceptional fundamental momentum, highlighted by a compounded profit growth of 81% over the trailing twelve months and a 38% surge in trailing sales growth [E16, E19]. The company's operational efficiency vastly outperforms sector benchmarks, delivering a robust ROCE of 25.22% compared to the sector median of 12.9%, alongside a superior ROE of 19.12% [E8, E9, E10]. Institutional confidence is firmly expanding as foreign and domestic institutions have steadily increased their holdings by +5.69 and +3.21 percentage points respectively since September 2023, driving positive money flow [E38, E39, E40]. Furthermore, the business is primed for sustained delivery with capital expenditure largely completed, evidenced by a -69.4% reduction in capital work-in-progress pointing to new capacity coming online [E36], all supported by a high-conviction rules-based screen score of 95 out of 100 [E59]. Conceded: the stock trades at a rich valuation with a P/E of 48.3x and a price-to-book ratio of 11.46x against sector benchmarks, while a discounted cash flow model suggests a negative margin of safety [E1, E2, E6, E7, E42].

R R Kabel Ltd trades at an exorbitant P/E ratio of 48.3 [E1] and a sector-dwarfing 50.68x [E6], alongside an EV/EBITDA of 30.75x compared to a sector benchmark of 12.72x [E11]. This multiple expansion is disconnected from fundamental value, as a discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at Rs 2191 per share against a market price of Rs 2614 [E41], resulting in a negative margin of safety of -19.3% [E42]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the current share price already demands an aggressive 20.4% earnings growth, outstripping the base case assumption of 18.0% [E43]. Expectations are running excessively ahead of delivery, with price growth exceeding profit growth by 26% [E53], while borrowings have ticked up to Rs 337 Cr [E35] and operating cash conversion sits at a moderate 0.60x of reported profit [E29]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong financial returns with an ROCE of 25.22% [E10] and robust recent profit growth [E19], backed by a positive sector tailwind score of 0.68 [E67].

Conceded: the discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at Rs 2191 against a market price of Rs 2614 [E41], and the reverse DCF demands an aggressive 20.4% earnings growth [E43]. However, those backward-looking models ignore the explosive acceleration in the business, demonstrated by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 38% [E16] and a staggering compounded profit growth of 81% [E19]. While the bear highlights borrowings of Rs 337 Cr [E35], the company maintains a conservatively financed debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.13x [E33]. Furthermore, the bear's focus on moderate cash conversion [E29] overlooks the robust operating cash flow of Rs 295 Cr generated in March 2026 [E30] and the completion of capital expenditure shown by CWIP dropping by 69.4% to Rs 72 Cr [E36], which frees up future capacity. Finally, the premium valuation multiples [E1, E6, E11] are fully justified by elite fundamentals, including an ROCE of 25.22% crushing the sector benchmark of 12.9% [E10], an ROE of 19.12% outperforming the sector's 10.84% [E9], and a top-tier rules-based screen score of 95 out of 100 [E59].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth reached 81% [E19], sales grew 38% over the same period [E16], and ROCE stands at an impressive 25.22% against a sector benchmark of 12.9% [E10]. However, pointing to an operating cash flow of Rs 295 Cr [E30] ignores the reality that cash conversion sits at a moderate 0.60x [E29] and operating cash flow represents only 57% of operating profit [E32], leaving free cash flow at a meager Rs 7 Cr [E31]. Dismissing the valuation misses the explicit warning from the reverse DCF that the current price already demands an aggressive 20.4% earnings growth—surpassing the base case of 18.0%—while leaving a negative margin of safety of -19.3% [E41, E42, E43]. Furthermore, the bull's reliance on recent momentum glosses over the reality that price growth has outpaced profit growth by 26% [E53], meaning expectations are running well ahead of delivery with a price-led setup [E52]. Finally, borrowings have ticked up to Rs 337 Cr from Rs 290 Cr a year earlier [E35], and promoter holding has steadily drifted lower by 1.38 percentage points down to 61.38% [E37].

Conceded: cash conversion sits at 0.60x [E29], free cash flow is Rs 7 Cr [E31], and the reverse DCF implies 20.4% earnings growth against an 18.0% base case with a negative margin of safety [E41, E42, E43]. Conceded: borrowings increased to Rs 337 Cr [E35] and promoter holdings drifted lower by 1.38 percentage points to 61.38% [E37]. However, the modest free cash flow coincides with a sharp drop in CWIP down 69.4%, proving that major capital expenditure has largely completed and new capacity is coming online [E36]. This newly deployed capital is supercharging delivery, backed by a rules-based screen scoring 95 out of 100 with high confidence [E59], alongside extraordinary TTM profit growth of 81% [E19] and sales growth of 38% [E16]. Furthermore, institutional conviction directly refutes any fear of runaway expectations, as foreign and domestic institutions have aggressively increased their stakes by +5.69 and +3.21 percentage points respectively [E38, E39], driving a positive institutional money flow signal [E40]. Finally, the capital goods sector tailwind score of +0.68 provides robust macroeconomic backing that validates the company's outperformance against sector medians in ROCE, ROE, sales growth, and profit growth [E8, E9, E10, E67, E68, E69].

While the bull cites the drop in CWIP [E36] as a catalyst, this transition has not yet yielded liquidity, as borrowings increased to Rs 337 Cr [E35] and free cash flow remains a negligible Rs 7 Cr [E31]. Conceded: the company has delivered strong profit growth [E19] and maintains superior ROCE and ROE [E10, E9, E8], but these achievements are aggressively priced at a P/E of 50.68x and P/B of 11.96x, both of which are more than double their sector benchmarks [E6, E7]. Institutional accumulation [E38, E39] has pushed the stock to 88% of its 52-week range [E44], resulting in price growth exceeding profit growth by 26% and signaling that expectations are running ahead of actual delivery [E53]. Even with a positive sector tailwind [E67], the company’s EV/EBITDA of 30.75x is nearly triple the sector benchmark of 12.72x [E11], confirming a valuation blind-spot where the current price already discounts the anticipated good news [E64].
